category_guides.1: An operable control (button, link, icon toggle) with no accessible name is ACC-A1A; an informational image, icon, chart or media item with no text alternative is ACC-A1B. Easy to confuse: an unlabeled form input is ACC-C1A, not ACC-A1A; a clickable div with no role is ACC-B1A even if it also lacks a name; a name that exists but is hardcoded outside the i18n layer is LNG-A1A.

A.guide: Semantics: whether elements expose what assistive technology needs to announce them, chiefly an accessible name for controls and a text alternative for informational non-text content. Category 1 holds the missing-name code (ACC-A1A) and the missing-alternative code (ACC-A1B).
A.name: semantics

category_guides.1: A div/span (or other non-interactive element) wired as a control without role and keyboard handling is ACC-B1A; a focusable control whose focus outline is removed with no visible replacement is ACC-B1B. The test that separates them: if the element cannot receive or act on keyboard input it is B1A; if it can but focus is invisible it is B1B. A native control that merely lacks a name is ACC-A1A.

B.guide: Keyboard: whether every control can be reached and operated without a pointer and whether the user can see where focus is. Category 1 holds the non-interactive-element-as-control code (ACC-B1A) and the suppressed-focus-indicator code (ACC-B1B).
B.name: keyboard

category_guides.1: A form input with no programmatically associated label (no <label for>, aria-label or aria-labelledby) is ACC-C1A, including a visible label that is not associated. A non-form control with no name is ACC-A1A; a validation error that appears but is never announced is ACC-D1A.

C.guide: Forms: whether form fields expose their purpose to assistive technology through a programmatic label. Category 1 holds the unlabeled-input code (ACC-C1A).
C.name: forms

category_guides.1: A dynamic status update rendered into the DOM with no aria-live or role=status/alert, and no focus move to it, is ACC-D1A. If the status is never rendered at all because the error was swallowed, that is a correctness defect (COD-B2C), not ACC; a field label missing from the start is ACC-C1A.

D.guide: Live regions: whether content that changes at runtime (errors, toasts, async results) is announced to screen-reader users. Category 1 holds the unannounced-status code (ACC-D1A).
D.name: live-regions

category_guides.1: Colour as the only cue for state, error, link or selection is ACC-E1A. An informational chart or icon that has no text alternative at all is ACC-A1B; low contrast ratio (WCAG 1.4.3/1.4.11) has no code in 0.6.0 and should not be forced into ACC-E1A.

E.guide: Contrast and perceivable distinction: whether information survives for users who cannot perceive colour differences. Category 1 currently holds only the colour-alone code (ACC-E1A); note there is no code yet for insufficient text or non-text contrast ratio despite the area name (see cross_domain_notes).
E.name: contrast

category_guides.1: Non-essential animation that ignores prefers-reduced-motion, or auto-playing motion with no pause control, is ACC-F1A. Flashing content (WCAG 2.3.1 seizure risk) has no code in 0.6.0 and is a different, more severe hazard; do not file it as ACC-F1A.

F.guide: Motion: whether animation and auto-playing movement respect the user's reduced-motion preference and can be stopped. Category 1 holds the reduced-motion code (ACC-F1A).
F.name: motion

ACC-A1A.criteria: Qualifies when an operable control (button, link, toggle, menu trigger), typically icon-only or graphic, exposes no programmatic accessible name (no text content, aria-label, aria-labelledby or title that the accessible-name computation resolves), so a screen-reader user hears only its role and cannot identify its purpose, violating WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Evidence names the control and the action it performs. A form input with no associated label is ACC-C1A; a div/span wired as a control without role or keyboard support is ACC-B1A (cite A1A only if the name is the sole missing piece); informational non-text content with no alternative is ACC-A1B; a name that exists but is a hardcoded untranslated string is LNG-A1A.
examples: icon-only-control-missing-accessible-name
icon-only-button-missing-accessible-name
ACC-A1A.name: icon-only-control-missing-accessible-name

lower_when.condition: A named, keyboard-reachable control performing the same action exists on the same view (e.g. an unlabeled toolbar icon duplicated by a labelled menu item), so the action is still discoverable to assistive-technology users.
The control is a secondary affordance whose action has no effect on task completion (e.g. a collapse/expand chevron on content that is also reachable unexpanded).

ACC-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when non-text content (image, icon, chart, media) conveys information but exposes no text alternative, so assistive-technology users lose it, violating WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content. Distinct from a control missing an accessible name (ACC-A1A); this is informational content, not an operable control.
examples: image-missing-alt-text
non-text-content-missing-text-alternative
ACC-A1B.name: non-text-content-missing-alternative

lower_when.condition: The same information is present as text adjacent to the image on the same view, so the defect is announcement noise (a filename or 'image' read aloud) rather than lost information; the correct fix is alt="".

raise_when.condition: The non-text content is the only carrier of information required to complete a task on that view (e.g. an image CAPTCHA with no alternative modality, or a chart whose values are needed to act and appear nowhere else as text), so an assistive-technology user cannot complete the task at all.

ACC-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when a div, span or other non-interactive element is wired as a control (click handler) without a native element or the full ARIA pattern (role, tabindex=0, and Enter/Space key handling), so keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot reach, identify or operate it, violating WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Evidence names the element and its handler. A native, focusable control whose focus is merely invisible is ACC-B1B; a native control that is operable but has no accessible name is ACC-A1A.
examples: div-clickable-lacks-role-and-tabindex
non-interactive-element-used-as-control
ACC-B1A.name: non-interactive-element-used-as-control

lower_when.condition: An equivalent native, keyboard-operable control for the same action exists on the same view, so keyboard users can still perform the action.
The element is focusable and keyboard-operable (tabindex and key handler present) but lacks only the role, so it works from the keyboard but is misannounced to screen readers.

ACC-B1B.criteria: Qualifies when the keyboard focus indicator is removed (e.g. outline:none) with no visible replacement, so keyboard users cannot see which element has focus, violating WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible. Distinct from a non-interactive element wired as a control (ACC-B1A); here the control is focusable but focus is invisible.
examples: focus-indicator-suppressed
outline-none-without-replacement
ACC-B1B.name: focus-indicator-suppressed

lower_when.condition: The suppression is limited to elements that receive focus only programmatically (tabindex=-1 containers such as a heading focused after route change), not tab-stop controls.

raise_when.condition: The suppression is a global selector (a base reset such as *:focus or :focus { outline: none }) that applies to every focusable element, with no :focus-visible or other visible replacement anywhere in the stylesheet, so the whole application is unusable for sighted keyboard users.

ACC-C1A.criteria: Qualifies when a form input (input, select, textarea, custom field) has no programmatically associated label (no <label for>/wrapping label, aria-label or aria-labelledby), so assistive technology cannot reliably announce the field's purpose, violating WCAG 1.3.1 and 4.1.2; includes a visible label not associated with the field and a placeholder used as the only label (placeholder is a fragile accessible-name fallback that disappears on input, WCAG 3.3.2). Evidence names the field. A non-form control missing its name is ACC-A1A; an error message for the field that appears but is never announced is ACC-D1A.
examples: form-input-label-not-programmatically-associated
placeholder-used-as-label
ACC-C1A.name: input-missing-programmatic-label

lower_when.condition: A persistent visible text label sits adjacent to the field and the field's title or aria-describedby exposes the same text, so the announced name matches the visible label and only the <label for>/aria-labelledby association is missing. A placeholder-only label stays at the default.

raise_when.condition: The field is a required input on the only path to complete a primary task (sign-in, checkout, submit) and exposes no accessible name at all (no label, placeholder, title or aria fallback), so a screen-reader user cannot complete the task.

ACC-D1A.criteria: Qualifies when a dynamic status change (validation error, toast, async result, loading completion) is rendered into the DOM without a live region (aria-live, role=status or role=alert) and without moving focus to it, so screen-reader users are never notified, violating WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages. Evidence names the update site and the missing announcement. A status that is never rendered at all because the underlying error was swallowed is COD-B2C; a field that was unlabeled from the start is ACC-C1A; a static control missing its name is ACC-A1A.
examples: status-toast-not-announced
dynamic-region-missing-aria-live
ACC-D1A.name: dynamic-status-not-announced

lower_when.condition: The status is a transient confirmation (e.g. 'Saved', 'Copied') whose outcome is verifiable from the state of the focused control or page, so no information needed to proceed is lost.

raise_when.condition: The unannounced change is a blocking error that prevents a primary task from completing (e.g. a submit rejected by validation) and focus does not move to it, so a screen-reader user cannot learn why the task failed or how to fix it.

ACC-E1A.criteria: Qualifies when colour is the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response or distinguishing an element (e.g. red-only error text, a link distinguished from body text only by hue, selection shown only by colour), so users who cannot perceive the colour lose the information, violating WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color. Evidence names the cue and the information it carries. Informational content with no text alternative at all is ACC-A1B; insufficient contrast ratio (WCAG 1.4.3/1.4.11) is not this code.
examples: selection-state-color-only
error-conveyed-by-color-alone
ACC-E1A.name: info-conveyed-by-color-alone

raise_when.condition: The colour-only cue is the sole indicator of a validation error, required field or destructive/irreversible state on a form or action the user must act on, so a user who cannot perceive the colour cannot tell what to fix or what will happen.

ACC-F1A.criteria: Qualifies when non-essential animation triggered by interaction or page state (transitions, parallax, scroll-linked or zoom/slide motion) runs without honouring the user's reduced-motion preference (prefers-reduced-motion), risking discomfort for motion-sensitive users, per WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions. Evidence names the animation and the missing preference check. Auto-playing motion lasting more than five seconds with no pause/stop control (WCAG 2.2.2) is the proposed split code; flashing content (WCAG 2.3.1) is not this code.
examples: animation-ignores-prefers-reduced-motion
autoplay-motion-no-user-control
ACC-F1A.name: motion-ignores-reduced-motion-preference

lower_when.condition: The animation is a brief non-positional transition (opacity or colour fade, no movement across the screen), which reduced-motion guidance does not require removing.

raise_when.condition: The motion auto-plays for more than five seconds alongside other content with no pause/stop/hide control (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A), or is a large-area vestibular trigger (parallax scrolling, full-viewport zoom/slide transition) with no reduced-motion branch.

ACC.guide: ACC (accessibility) covers user-facing defects that stop people using assistive technology (screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, reduced-motion settings) or with perceptual differences (colour vision, motion sensitivity) from perceiving or operating the UI, each tied to a WCAG success criterion. Choose ACC over QAL for any UI regression that is an assistive-technology defect (SCHEMA routing: ACC exclusively owns these); choose LNG instead when the problem is translation, locale formatting or text direction, even if the string is an aria-label or alt text. Look in A (semantics) for missing names and text alternatives, B (keyboard) for operability and visible focus, C (forms) for unlabeled inputs, D (live-regions) for unannounced runtime changes, E (contrast) for colour-only information, and F (motion) for animation that ignores user preference.
ACC.name: accessibility

category_guides.1: AGT-A1A needs demonstrated steering (an injection payload or its effect); AGT-A1B is the exposure precursor where untrusted content reaches the context with no steering shown. Untrusted text rendered unescaped into HTML or Markdown output, with no model involved, is SEC-B1C, not this category.

A.guide: Untrusted content (reviewed files, issue and PR text, fetched web pages, tool results and MCP server responses, other agents' output) that reaches an agent's prompt or context. Category 1 splits by evidence: a demonstrated steering attempt or effect (AGT-A1A) versus exposure alone (AGT-A1B).
A.name: prompt-injection-surfaces

category_guides.1: An existing control that misses a class of invocations is AGT-B1A; no human approval on a destructive action is AGT-B1B; a write tool that can act outside its intended path, repo or tenant is AGT-B1C; a tool set larger than the task needs is AGT-B1D. B1C and B1D are the pair most often confused (depth of one grant versus breadth of the set). A control that fails open when its own config is missing is ARC-F2E, one that mis-parses an invocation is ARC-F2C, and a hook that cannot tell actors apart is ARC-F2B. Ambient-authority mutation by ordinary code is SEC-C1D, and a non-agent shared guard that is too broad is COD-B1C.

B.guide: What an agent is allowed to do: tool grants, write scope, approval gates, and the enforcement hooks that mediate tool calls. Category 1 is routed by what is absent: an incomplete control, a missing approval gate, a missing scope bound, or too many tools.
B.name: tool-and-permission-scoping

category_guides.1: An agent-authored record that asserts its own trust fields (corroborated, source, cvss) is AGT-C1A; output from an undeclared source that is detected but still merged is AGT-C1B; a trust mapping rebuilt from unauthenticated external text (issue bodies) is AGT-C1C; leniently parsed free-text LLM output that drives a control decision is AGT-C1D. C1A and C1D are easy to confuse: C1A is a structured field that claims trust, C1D is unvalidated parsing of prose.

C.guide: Trust boundaries on agent-produced or agent-adjacent output: fields, files, mappings and free text that the pipeline accepts as trusted without verifying them. Category 1 is routed by what is trusted: a self-asserted field, a whole record from an undeclared source, a mapping rebuilt from external text, or leniently parsed prose.
C.name: output-trust-boundaries

category_guides.1: A reported action or result that the execution record does not support, accepted unchecked, is AGT-D1A; a secret written by the agent into a persisted or published output is AGT-D1B; one verifier's verdict that can override other evidence alone is AGT-D1C. A leniently parsed verdict is AGT-C1D, not D1C; a secret sent to the provider in a prompt is AGT-F1A, not D1B.

D.guide: Oversight of what an agent claims, decides, or emits: reported actions that never happened, secrets the agent writes into its outputs, and verifier verdicts that carry unchecked authority. Category 1 points at those three codes.
D.name: autonomy-and-oversight

category_guides.1: No iteration cap, deadline or independent termination condition is AGT-E1A; a terminating run with no cap on total tool calls, tokens or spend is AGT-E1B. Generic unbounded memory, connection or CPU use is OPS-D1A; retries with no backoff are OPS-A1B.

E.guide: Termination and spend bounds on agent runs. Category 1 splits a loop that may never end from a run that ends but has no cap on tool calls, tokens, or cost.
E.name: resource-and-cost-safety

category_guides.1: Sensitive data in a prompt or context sent to a third-party provider is AGT-F1A. A secret the agent writes into its own report, comment or commit is AGT-D1B; secrets or PII written to logs by ordinary code are SEC-B2B or SEC-B4A.

F.guide: Data the agent sends out of the trust boundary to a model provider in prompts, context, or tool results. Category 1 holds the provider-egress code.
F.name: data-egress

AGT-A1A.criteria: Qualifies when indirect prompt injection is DEMONSTRATED — untrusted content reaches the agent context AND provably attempts to steer the agent (an injection payload / instruction-like content aimed at the model), not merely present. The evidentiary bar is shown steering intent or effect. Untrusted content that reaches the context WITHOUT demonstrated steering is the exposure precursor AGT-A1B. Mitigations that neutralise the steering — delimiter/where-escaping, quoting untrusted content, output fencing — demote an instance toward AGT-A1B or justify a consumer severity_modifier (`compensating-control-present`).
examples: Reviewer agent prompt templates never tell the model that reviewed file content is untrusted
Advisor prompt embeds an unfiltered agent-authored finding JSON, opening an indirect-prompt-injection channel
AGT-A1A.name: indirect-prompt-injection-untrusted-content-in-agent-context

lower_when.condition: the steered agent has no write, execute or egress tool, AND its output is adjudicated by a separate trusted step before any decision, so the steering can at worst skew one advisory output

raise_when.condition: the injection payload can be authored by an unauthenticated external party (a public PR, issue, comment or fetched web page), AND the instruction it carries targets a shell-execution, unsandboxed-write or network-egress tool that the steered agent holds and that runs with no human approval

AGT-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when untrusted content (reviewed file text, issue or PR bodies, fetched pages, tool results or MCP responses, another agent's output) reaches an agent's prompt or context but no steering attempt or effect is demonstrated. Evidence names the untrusted source and the prompt or context site it reaches. Delimiting, quoting or an untrusted-data instruction does not disqualify the instance; it lowers it. When an injection payload or its effect is shown, the code is AGT-A1A. Untrusted text rendered unescaped into generated HTML or Markdown output, with no model consuming it, is SEC-B1C.
AGT-A1B.name: untrusted-content-in-agent-context

lower_when.condition: the content reaches only a tool-less, single-shot model call whose output is shown to a human and is not parsed into any decision or action
the untrusted content is fenced or quoted as data AND the prompt instructs the model that it is untrusted, AND the consuming agent has no write, execute or egress tool

AGT-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when a mediation/enforcement mechanism EXISTS but fails to cover a class of invocations — a coverage gap in the control itself (e.g. a write-guard that gates Write/Edit but not Bash). Axis: an existing-but-incomplete control is always B1A; where NO control mediates the action, route by what is absent — missing human approval on a destructive action is B1B, absent scope bounds on a write-capable tool is B1C, and an over-broad grant of tools beyond the task is B1D. A control that runs but mis-parses an undocumented input shape is instead ARC-F2C. Severity is graded by the CAPABILITY of the ungated invocation class, not the mere existence of the gap: HIGH when that class can write, execute, or exfiltrate (an ungated Bash/Edit/Write, or any path to un-adjudicated egress); MEDIUM when the ungated class is read-only and its output is adjudicated — e.g. a review scope-fence constraining Read/Grep/Glob only, with no write/exec/egress channel — especially where the gap is disclosed.
examples: Write-guard covers only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit tool_name calls
AGT-B1A.name: incomplete-mediation-coverage-gap

lower_when.condition: the ungated invocation class is read-only (e.g. Read/Grep/Glob) and its output is adjudicated by a trusted step, with no write, execute or egress channel (as the entry's criteria already state)

AGT-B1B.criteria: Qualifies when an agent can trigger a destructive or irreversible action (deleting files, branches or data, force-pushing over shared history, merging to a protected branch, spending money, sending external messages) with no human approval checkpoint on the path at all. The gate is absent, not incomplete. Evidence names the action, the tool or call that performs it, and the path that reaches it with no checkpoint. A mediating control that exists but misses a class of invocations is AGT-B1A; a write tool with no scope bound is AGT-B1C; too many tools granted is AGT-B1D. A sensitive action with no audit record (agent or not) is SEC-C4B.
AGT-B1B.name: missing-approval-gate-for-destructive-action

lower_when.condition: the destructive action is confined to an ephemeral sandbox, worktree or scratch branch that the agent created for this run and that nothing else reads

raise_when.condition: the ungated destructive action targets shared production state that has no backup or other copy (a production database without restorable backups, cloud resources, other users' records), AND the same agent ingests content that an unauthenticated external party can author (public PR, issue, comment or fetched page)

AGT-B1C.criteria: Qualifies when a granted write-capable tool can act OUTSIDE its intended scope (path/namespace/repo/tenant) — scope is absent, not merely broad. If instead the grant includes more tools than the task needs (breadth), that is AGT-B1D; if a mediating control exists but misses a class of invocations, AGT-B1A; if a destructive action has no approval gate at all, AGT-B1B.
AGT-B1C.name: unscoped-write-authority

lower_when.condition: the out-of-scope reach stays inside the same repository or tenant that the agent's principal is already allowed to write, and cannot reach another tenant, repository, system path or credential store

AGT-B1D.criteria: Qualifies when the granted tool SET exceeds what the declared task requires (breadth of grant), even if each tool is individually scoped. If a single write tool lacks scope bounds (can act outside its intended path/tenant), that is AGT-B1C; if a destructive action has no approval checkpoint, AGT-B1B; if an existing mediation control has a coverage gap, AGT-B1A.
AGT-B1D.name: overbroad-tool-grant

lower_when.condition: every tool beyond the task's needs is read-only and confined to the task's own inputs (e.g. an extra Grep alongside a granted Read)

raise_when.condition: at least one excess tool can execute shell commands, write outside the task scope, or reach the network and runs with no human approval, AND the same agent ingests content that an unauthenticated external party can author (public PR, issue, comment or fetched page)

AGT-C1A.criteria: [audit text unchanged up to '...free-text LLM output parsed leniently into a decision is AGT-C1D;'] an agent's unchecked prose claim that it performed an action or verification, with no self-asserted field, is AGT-D1A.
examples: Self-asserted corroborated/corroborated_by fields bypass agent-trust sanitization and forge cross-panel verification
Self-asserted source/reinforced fields let an agent finding forge tool_confirmed evidence
Agent-authored `cvss`/`exploit_scenario` unconditionally overwrite a tool-verified finding's own metadata
Self-asserted `corroborated`/`corroborated_by` fields let an untrusted reviewer finding forge verification status
Self-asserted _group field can misattribute a finding to the wrong review group

corroborated/corroborated_by are self-assertable by agents even though the semantically-equivalent source/reinforced fields are explicitly stripped as forbidden, allowing spoofed cross-panel corroboration
AGT-C1A.name: self-asserted-trust-metadata-spoofing

lower_when.condition: the spoofable field changes only display, grouping or ordering (e.g. a _group attribution) and cannot change a gate verdict, suppression, severity, or verification status

AGT-C1B.criteria: Qualifies when the pipeline detects that an agent-produced record came from an undeclared or unexpected source (an unregistered output file, an unknown producer, a path outside the dispatch plan) and records that detection (an integrity flag, a warning), yet still merges the record into trusted output with full weight. The defect is detection without enforcement. Evidence names the detection point and the merge that ignores it. A record that forges its own trust fields is AGT-C1A. A stated policy or verdict that no code enforces, with no agent-output detection involved, is ARC-F1E.
examples: Findings from an undeclared/unexpected findings file are flagged in meta.integrity
AGT-C1B.name: findings-from-undeclared-source-merged-despite-flagging

lower_when.condition: the merged records can only add new findings (never remove, downgrade or verify others), and the integrity flag appears next to them in the delivered report

raise_when.condition: the merged records can remove, suppress, downgrade or mark as verified another source's findings, or flip the gate verdict, AND the integrity flag is not surfaced to the gate or in the delivered report

AGT-C1C.criteria: Qualifies when a trust mapping that later decisions rely on (fingerprint to issue, finding to ticket, identity to record) is rebuilt or recovered from external content that parties outside the trust boundary can write (issue or PR body text, comments, remote metadata), with no check of the author or of the content against a trusted record, so a third party can redirect or forge the mapping. Evidence names the external source, the recovery path, and the decision the mapping feeds. Agent-authored fields asserting their own trust are AGT-C1A; information lost in a producer-to-recovery round trip is ARC-D1A; a fingerprint that is unstable across runs is ARC-D1C.
examples: recover-linkage rebuilds the fingerprint-to-issue trust mapping from unauthenticated issue body text
Ledger recovery trusts unauthenticated GitHub issue-body content to rebuild the fingerprint-to-issue linkage
AGT-C1C.name: unauthenticated-external-data-rebuilds-trust-mapping

lower_when.condition: a wrong mapping can only cause a duplicate issue or a lost link, never a suppressed, closed or resolved finding

raise_when.condition: the external text can be written by any user who is not a collaborator (e.g. issue bodies on a public repository), AND the rebuilt mapping can close, suppress or mark as resolved a finding or issue

AGT-C1D.criteria: [audit text unchanged up to '...is AGT-D1C.'] A non-enforcement component that skips or tolerates malformed non-LLM input is ARC-F2D; a hidden format contract enforced only by a regex is ARC-A2B.
examples: Advisor verdict ingestion trusts lenient, unauthenticated free-text LLM output
AGT-C1D.name: unstructured-llm-output-trusted-for-control-decision

lower_when.condition: the parsed output only annotates or ranks, and a parse failure rejects the output rather than defaulting to a verdict

raise_when.condition: the parsed decision can suppress or downgrade findings or approve an action with write or execute effect, AND unparseable or unrecognised output defaults to the permissive outcome (pass, suppress, approve) rather than rejecting

AGT-D1A.criteria: Qualifies when a pipeline accepts an agent's report that it performed an action or obtained a result (tests run, file written, claim verified, tool called) without checking the report against the execution or tool-call record, and the record shows that the action did not happen or produced a different result. Evidence names the claim, the consuming step, and the missing or contradicting record. A structured trust field the agent asserts about itself (corroborated, tool_confirmed) is AGT-C1A; free-text output parsed into a decision is AGT-C1D; an enforcement check that reads a stale persisted flag instead of verifying live state is ARC-F1A.
AGT-D1A.name: agent-confabulated-action

lower_when.condition: the accepted claim appears only in a narrative summary and no downstream step (gate, merge, verdict, status update) consumes it

AGT-D1B.criteria: [audit text unchanged, with the SEC-B2C clause replaced by:] when a redaction pass exists on the agent's output channel and misses the secret, the finding is SEC-B2C; D1B is for an agent output channel with no redaction at all.
AGT-D1B.name: secret-materialized-into-agent-output

lower_when.condition: the output channel is a local run artifact that is never committed, uploaded, posted or shipped off the machine

AGT-D1C.criteria: Qualifies when one model's or verifier's verdict alone can override, suppress or clear findings or evidence from other sources (tool confirmations, multiple reviewers) with no corroboration, quorum, tie-break or human check, so a single wrong or steered verdict flips the outcome. Evidence names the verdict source and the evidence it can override. A verdict whose free-text output is parsed leniently is AGT-C1D; an agent asserting its own corroboration is AGT-C1A; a CI gate that bypasses the domain verdict model is ARC-C1A; a stated verdict policy that no code enforces is ARC-F1E.
examples: Evidence model gives a single advisor-LLM verdict unilateral, uncorroborated power
AGT-D1C.name: single-verifier-unilateral-override-authority

lower_when.condition: the single verdict can only add or upgrade findings and can never suppress, downgrade or clear one

raise_when.condition: the single verdict can clear a tool-confirmed finding or a HIGH or CRITICAL finding from the gating verdict, AND the cleared finding is not listed, with the overriding verdict, in the delivered report

AGT-E1A.criteria: Qualifies when an agent's plan-act-observe, retry or self-correction loop has no iteration cap, wall-clock deadline, or termination condition independent of the model's own judgment, so a model that never declares itself done runs indefinitely. Evidence names the loop and the missing bound. A loop that terminates but has no cap on total tool calls, tokens or spend is AGT-E1B; unbounded memory, connections or CPU use in ordinary code is OPS-D1A; retries with no backoff or jitter are OPS-A1B.
AGT-E1A.name: unbounded-agent-loop

lower_when.condition: every iteration blocks on a human message or approval, so the loop cannot run unattended

AGT-E1B.criteria: Qualifies when an agent run has no cap on total tool calls, tokens or spend (per run, per session or per trigger), even though its loop terminates, so one task can consume unbounded cost or exhaust a shared rate limit. Evidence names the run entry point and the missing budget. A loop with no termination bound at all is AGT-E1A; unbounded resource use in ordinary code is OPS-D1A.
AGT-E1B.name: unbounded-tool-call-budget

lower_when.condition: the only uncapped dimension is free local tool calls (file reads, local search) with no billed, metered or rate-limited call

raise_when.condition: the run is started by an event an unauthenticated party can trigger (a public PR, issue comment or webhook) with no maintainer-approval gate or per-trigger rate limit, and spends against a billed or quota-limited account

AGT-F1A.criteria: Qualifies when sensitive data (secrets, credentials, personal data, regulated or customer data) is included in a prompt, context or tool result sent to a third-party model provider with no redaction, minimization or declared data-processing basis. Evidence names the data source and the call that sends it. A secret the agent writes into its own persisted or published output is AGT-D1B; secrets or personal data written to logs by ordinary code are SEC-B2B or SEC-B4A; a redaction pass that exists but misses a pattern is SEC-B2C; collecting more data than needed at the source is SEC-B4B.
AGT-F1A.name: sensitive-data-sent-to-model-provider

lower_when.condition: the only sensitive data sent is the operator's own identifiers (username, local paths, hostname)

raise_when.condition: the payload contains credentials read from environment variables or credential files, or health or payment records about people other than the operator, AND the request or client config enables provider-side retention, logging or training use (or targets a consumer or free tier that does)

AGT.guide: AGT covers hazards that exist because an LLM agent is in the loop: untrusted content reaching the model's context (A), what the agent's tools are allowed to do (B), agent output trusted without verification (C), unchecked agent claims, verdicts and secret-bearing outputs (D), unbounded agent loops and spend (E), and data sent to a model provider (F). Choose SEC when the same defect would exist with no model involved (classic injection, credentials printed by ordinary code, missing authorization, ambient-authority mutation). Choose ARC when the defect is in the design of an enforcement control rather than in the agent's grant: a compensating control with a blind spot (ARC-F2A), a hook that cannot scope to an individual actor (ARC-F2B), a control that mis-parses input (ARC-F2C), or a control that fails open on misconfiguration (ARC-F2E). Choose OPS for generic resource overload, timeouts and retries.
AGT.name: agentic-trust

category_guides.1: Cohesion: ARC-A1A when one rule is scattered across many units with no owner, ARC-A1B when one module holds many unrelated jobs, ARC-A1C when one function mixes separable concerns. A long function with a single concern is QAL-H1A.
category_guides.2: Coupling: ARC-A2A for cyclic or import-order dependencies, ARC-A2B when producer and consumer share a grammar defined only by a parser, ARC-A2C for sys.path hacks standing in for a package layout (test-suite form TST-G1A; per-instance QAL-F1A), ARC-A2D for a public surface that leaks internals.
category_guides.3: Duplication with a structural gap, where the fix must create a shared home: ARC-A3A for business logic with no shared module, ARC-A3B for a configuration or mapping table defined in several places. A scalar constant with no canonical owner is ARC-A5A and a mechanically derivable copy is ARC-A5B; per-instance duplicates fixable in place are QAL-D1A/QAL-D1B/QAL-D1C.
category_guides.4: Extension-point consistency: ARC-A4A for an outlier adapter that breaks the siblings' convention (declared-protocol violations are COD-D3B), ARC-A4C for a hand-kept shadow registry with no enforced parity (retired-but-registered is QAL-E2B), and ARC-A4D for silently ignoring an unregistered key (compare ARC-F2D, COD-C3B).
category_guides.5: Canonical ownership: ARC-A5A for a constant with no authoritative owner (per-instance is QAL-D1B), ARC-A5B for a structure kept by hand though it could be derived. Check ARC-A3B and ARC-A2B before choosing.

A.guide: Module boundaries: how code is divided into units, who owns each rule, constant or registry, and how units depend on each other. Use A1 for cohesion, A2 for coupling, A3 and A5 for duplication and missing canonical owners, and A4 for consistency across implementations of a shared extension point. A per-instance copy-paste fixable in place is QAL-D1x, not A.
A.name: module-boundaries

category_guides.1: Packaging metadata: ARC-B1A for undeclared runtime dependencies, ARC-B1D for a missing build-system declaration, ARC-B1C for stale manifest URLs (doc/code URLs are QAL-C1A), ARC-B1E for lint config that disables its own rule, and ARC-B1F for install paths that bypass the package manager.
category_guides.3: Container image and environment design: ARC-B3A when tested and shipped environments differ (per-host config parity is ARC-E3C), ARC-B3B for one image holding many unrelated toolchains, and ARC-B3C for images built FROM another mutable in-repo image. Container privilege is SEC-C1A/SEC-C1E.

B.guide: Dependency and build architecture: whether the packaging manifest describes an installable project and whether container images are designed well. Use B1 for manifests and install mechanics and B3 for image and environment design. Pinning, integrity and supply-chain risk belong to SEC-E.
B.name: dependency-and-build-architecture

category_guides.1: Pipeline gating: ARC-C1A when a gate bypasses the project's verdict model, ARC-C1B when trigger paths miss consumed inputs, ARC-C1D when lint globs exclude in-scope code, ARC-C1C when integration tests never run against real tools (mocked/absent tests are TST-A3A), ARC-C1E for a missing least-privilege permissions block, and ARC-C1F when generated artifacts are never regenerated and diffed.
category_guides.2: Failure handling: ARC-C2A when a failing step silently falls back to another path, ARC-C2B when a step simply ignores its own failure. Scan tools that silently lose coverage are SEC-G2B.

C.guide: CI/CD pipeline architecture: whether the pipeline gates on the right signal, covers the right inputs, and surfaces its own failures. Use C1 for what a gate checks and when it runs, and C2 for failures the pipeline hides. Test-quality defects inside the suite are TST; supply-chain pinning is SEC-E2x.
C.name: ci-cd-pipeline-architecture

category_guides.1: Schema-implementation drift: ARC-D1B for wholesale doc-vs-schema divergence (field-level is COD-D1A/COD-D1D), ARC-D1D for one id format specified differently across artifacts (COD-D1B when live output is rejected), ARC-D1A for lossy producer/recovery round trips, ARC-D1C for unstable fingerprints, ARC-D1E for one fact derived independently without reconciliation, and ARC-D1F for unversioned inter-phase artifacts (persisted formats are DAT-F2A).
category_guides.2: Contract completeness: ARC-D2A for systemic CLI contract drift (one unimplemented flag is COD-D2B, stale flag docs are QAL-C2C), ARC-D2E for a required field no producer emits vs ARC-D2D for an optional field never populated, ARC-D2F for undefined terms, ARC-D2C for agents sharing state with no coordination contract, and ARC-D2B for equivalent inputs handled differently.
category_guides.3: Missing referenced artifacts: ARC-D3A when code or build references an absent file and something breaks, ARC-D3B when docs assert a structural artifact the repo lacks. A drifted path pointer that breaks nothing is QAL-C1C.

D.guide: Contracts and interfaces: agreement between schemas, specs, prompts, CLIs and the code that produces or consumes them. Use D1 when an implementation or identity drifts from its schema, D2 when a contract is incomplete or ambiguous, and D3 when a referenced artifact is missing. When one output instance is rejected or wrong, route to COD-C3x/COD-D1x instead.
D.name: contracts-and-interfaces

category_guides.1: Hardcoded values: ARC-E1A for machine-specific absolute paths in shipped source (fixture data is TST-E2C), ARC-E1B for a path tied to one run or date, and ARC-E1C for one identifier hardcoded independently in several modules (a single stale URL is QAL-C1A or ARC-B1C).
category_guides.2: Implicit and global state: ARC-E2A for durable records kept in a disposable location, ARC-E2B for global writes in a project-scoped model, ARC-E2C for a documented runtime precondition nothing checks (compare ARC-F1E), and ARC-E2D for silent config auto-discovery (compare QAL-C2F).
category_guides.3: Config-model complexity: ARC-E3A for config axes whose cross-product is never enumerated or validated, ARC-E3C for per-host config that lacks parity across hosts (CI-vs-image environment divergence is ARC-B3A), and ARC-E3B for a peer component lacking reference material its siblings have (an incomplete docs inventory is ARC-G1C).

E.guide: Configuration architecture: hardcoded values that should be configuration, implicit or global state, and configuration models too complex to reason about. Use E1 for hardcoding, E2 for implicit and global state, and E3 for configuration-model complexity and parity. Config-loader fail-direction bugs are COD-B1A; startup validation is OPS-C1A.
E.name: configuration-architecture

category_guides.1: Enforcement gaps: ARC-F1E when a documented policy has no code enforcing it (an unchecked environmental precondition such as the working directory is ARC-E2C), ARC-F1A when enforcement trusts a stale flag, ARC-F1C when only some sibling scripts check authorization, ARC-F1B when audit accounting skips in-scope actors, and ARC-F1D when a batch operation has no recovery path for a mid-batch failure (a non-atomic compound operation is COD-F1A).
category_guides.2: Fail-open defaults and control blind spots: ARC-F2E when a security control permits because its own config is missing or malformed, ARC-F2D when a non-enforcement component skips malformed input (config-loader form COD-B1A, scan-tool form SEC-G2B), ARC-F2C when a control mis-parses an input shape, ARC-F2A when a compensating control exempts the critical scope, ARC-F2B when a hook cannot tell actors apart, and ARC-F2G for structurally overbroad catches (security swallow SEC-F1B, single unchecked failure COD-B2C).

F.guide: Enforcement and security boundary: the architecture of gates, guards and policies. Did enforcement happen, did it cover the right scope, and which way does it fail? Use F1 when a stated policy or authorization is not enforced or is enforced on stale data, and F2 for controls that fail open or have blind spots. A control that misses a whole class of agent invocations is AGT-B1A; an exploit primitive is SEC.
F.name: enforcement-and-security-boundary

category_guides.1: Doc-reality drift: ARC-G1B when two sources of truth for one fact diverge, ARC-G1A when contributor instructions differ from CI, and ARC-G1C when reference docs omit existing components (a capability with no docs at all is COD-D2D).
category_guides.2: Design-doc lifecycle: ARC-G2A for a superseded doc with no deprecation marker, ARC-G2B for a doc still presented as current that has drifted from what was delivered.
category_guides.3: Repo hygiene and meta-config: ARC-G3B for files tracked against the repo's own ignore rules. A tracked file that leaks a secret is SEC-B3A.

G.guide: Documentation and spec integrity at the repository level: docs that disagree with code or CI, design docs whose lifecycle state is unclear, and the repository's own meta-configuration. Use G1 for disagreements between sources, G2 for superseded or drifted design docs, and G3 for repo hygiene. A single document contradicting itself is QAL-C2B; inert stale pointers are QAL-C1x.
G.name: documentation-and-spec-integrity

ARC-A1A.criteria: Qualifies when one coherent rule or policy (a precedence order, a lifecycle, a template-management duty) has no single owning function or module and is instead implied by fragments spread across several, so no one site states the rule and every change must touch all fragments. When the fragments are literal copies of the same logic, that is ARC-A3A (structural) or QAL-D1A (per-instance); when one module holds many unrelated responsibilities rather than one rule being spread out, that is ARC-A1B.
examples: Evidence status precedence hierarchy (verdict > corroboration > tool_source, reinforced handling) is implicit and scattered across multiple functions instead of centralized
Template management scattered across multiple functions with no single owner
ARC-A1A.name: fragmented-logic-no-single-owner

lower_when.condition: All fragments live in one module and a single comment or docstring states the full rule and names every site that implements part of it.

ARC-A1B.criteria: Qualifies when a single MODULE or class owns several unrelated responsibilities (discovery, parsing, execution, reporting) with no internal boundary, so a change to one concern risks the others. When the mixing is inside one FUNCTION, that is ARC-A1C; a long function with a single concern is QAL-H1A; one rule scattered across modules (rather than many rules in one module) is ARC-A1A.
examples: Monolithic dispatch.py module violates single responsibility principle (template loading, frontmatter parsing, model resolution, plan emission all in one ~687-line module)
orchestrator.py/evidence.py/run_tools.py/synthesize.py each mix file discovery, pattern matching, execution, and reporting concerns with no internal boundary
ARC-A1B.name: mixed-responsibility-module

lower_when.condition: The module is an entry point or composition root whose only job is wiring the concerns together, and each concern is already delegated to its own function or module.

ARC-A1C.criteria: Qualifies when a function mixes SEPARABLE concerns that belong in different units — a structural/boundary problem whose fix extracts distinct responsibilities into separate modules or functions. When the function has a SINGLE concern but is simply too long or complex, that is QAL-H1A.
examples: Monolithic main() violates single responsibility principle
Rendering function mixes data transformation and HTML generation
Complex directory-walking logic combines discovery, filtering, and pattern matching in one routine
ARC-A1C.name: monolithic-function-mixed-concerns

lower_when.condition: The function is a top-level main() or orchestrator in which each concern is a single delegated call (it sequences concerns but implements none of them).

ARC-A2A.criteria: Qualifies when two or more modules depend on each other cyclically (held together by a deferred or function-local import), or when correctness depends on module import ORDER (registration side effects at load time), so reordering or isolating an import breaks the program. A cyclic or chained BUILD/image dependency is ARC-B3C; a one-way dependency on another module's internals is ARC-A2D; an inline import flagged only for placement is QAL-B1B.
examples: Circular module dependency between dispatch.py and orchestrator.py held together only by a deferred import
Tool adapter registration tightly coupled at module load time
Direct ADAPTERS registry import creates tight coupling between synthesize and domain modules
ARC-A2A.name: circular-or-load-order-coupling

lower_when.condition: The cycle exists only through a type-checking-only import (e.g. under TYPE_CHECKING) and creates no runtime dependency.

ARC-A2B.criteria: Qualifies when a producer and a consumer share a data or naming grammar (a filename pattern, a key format, a panel list) whose ONLY specification is an informal parser such as a regex or a byte-for-byte reimplementation, with no shared definition both import. When the same id/format is formally specified in several artifacts that disagree, that is ARC-D1D; when the issue is only that a constant list lacks a canonical owner, that is ARC-A5A; when the two sides have already diverged so live output is dropped or mismatched, cite the COD instance (e.g. COD-C2C, COD-C2D).
examples: group_runner.py's _OUTFILE_RE regex is the only specification of the group/panel filename grammar shared between producer and consumer modules
reconcile_apply.ledger_key() must byte-for-byte match file_issues.key_for() with no shared source of truth
Panel names require manual synchronization in a regex pattern maintained separately from the panel registry
ARC-A2B.name: hidden-contract-via-informal-parsing

lower_when.condition: Producer and consumer live in the same module, or a test round-trips producer output through the consumer's parser.

ARC-A2C.criteria: Qualifies when production entry points find sibling modules by mutating sys.path (or an equivalent import-path hack) because the code is not laid out as an installable package. This is a structural packaging gap whose fix is a proper package layout. The same hack confined to the test suite is TST-G1A; a single implicit import dependency fixable in place is QAL-F1A; third-party imports missing from the manifest are ARC-B1A.
examples: sys.path.insert(0, ...) in dispatch.py to import sibling modules instead of a proper package layout
Ad hoc sys.path bootstrap duplicated verbatim across three entry-point scripts
Inconsistent sys.path manipulation and import-fallback patterns across the codebase undermine installability
ARC-A2C.name: unpackaged-module-resolution-hack

lower_when.condition: The hack sits in a single standalone script that no other module imports and that is not an installed entry point.

ARC-A2D.criteria: Qualifies when a module's public surface exposes or re-exports another module's internals, or a shared tool-agnostic helper embeds caller-specific policy, so consumers couple to implementation details. When the coupling is cyclic or depends on import order, that is ARC-A2A; when producer and consumer share a grammar defined only by a parser, that is ARC-A2B.
examples: Public module re-exports internal implementation details via __all__, coupling the public surface to another module's internals
Module aliasing functions from another module without an explicit interface contract
Tool-specific noise-filtering policy (bandit B101 suppression) embedded directly in a shared, tool-agnostic helper
ARC-A2D.name: leaky-module-interface

lower_when.condition: The leaked names are underscore-prefixed or documented as unstable, and no caller outside the package imports them.

ARC-A3A.criteria: Qualifies when duplicated business logic reveals a STRUCTURAL gap — there is no shared module or owner where the logic belongs, so a proper fix must introduce a canonical home that multiple call sites depend on (an ownership or boundary change). When the finding is simply that a block of logic is copy-pasted and should be consolidated within the existing structure (per-instance), that is QAL-D1A.
examples: gh-retry-with-backoff and ledger-persistence logic reimplemented independently in three separate scripts
Finding-construction boilerplate copy-pasted across nine tool adapters instead of one shared builder in base.py
html_report's compare-mode fingerprint reimplements (and regresses) synthesize's already-fixed finding-identity logic
ARC-A3A.name: duplicated-business-logic-without-shared-module

lower_when.condition: Exactly two copies exist inside one package and a single test exercises both against the same expected output.

ARC-A3B.criteria: Qualifies when a configuration or mapping TABLE (role-to-file map, glob, model policy) is defined in two or more places with no single source of truth, so an edit to one copy silently misses the other. A scalar constant with no canonical owner is ARC-A5A; a second table mechanically derivable from the first is ARC-A5B; a per-instance duplicate constant fixable in place is QAL-D1B.
examples: Role-to-filename mappings defined in two places (ROLE_FILES and AGENT_NAME) with no single source of truth
dispatch-plan*.json glob duplicated verbatim across two functions with a documented history of drifting apart
Model policy hardcoded and duplicated across dispatch.py and model_resolver.py
ARC-A3B.name: duplicated-configuration-or-mapping-table

lower_when.condition: Both copies are defined in the same function or the same literal block, so one edit visibly touches both.

raise_when.condition: The copies already disagree on at least one key or value and both copies are read on a live code path (cite ARC-G1B alongside for the realized divergence).

ARC-A4A.criteria: Qualifies when one implementation of a shared extension point (adapter, plugin, handler) departs from the convention every sibling follows (parsing style, defaulting direction, input format), so the outlier behaves differently on the same class of input. When the outlier violates an explicitly DECLARED protocol or interface, that is COD-D3B; when the deviation is an unhardened XML parse, the security hazard is SEC-A4A.
examples: pip_audit.parse() indexes dict keys directly, breaking the .get()-with-default convention every sibling adapter uses
cargo_audit defaults missing-CVSS advisories to HIGH, the opposite fail-safe direction used elsewhere in the same file set
spotbugs.py is the only adapter parsing tool output with un-hardened stdlib XML instead of JSON/SARIF like its siblings
ARC-A4A.name: adapter-implementation-inconsistency

lower_when.condition: The deviation is stylistic only: the outlier produces the same observable result as its siblings on every input, including missing keys.

ARC-A4C.criteria: Qualifies when a hand-maintained list or registry mirrors an authoritative registry and no test or derivation enforces parity, so entries can be added to one and missed in the other. A component removed from use but still registered is QAL-E2B; a second structure fully derivable from the first is ARC-A5B.
examples: PROBES is a hand-maintained shadow of the ADAPTERS registry with no enforced parity; live adapters have shipped without a matching probe entry
ARC-A4C.name: shadow-registry-without-enforced-parity

lower_when.condition: A parity check exists but runs only outside CI (manual script or pre-release checklist).

ARC-A4D.criteria: Qualifies when an extension point (format registry, host/role resolver, plugin lookup) meets a key it has no registration for and silently skips or returns None instead of raising or logging, so the missing registration cannot be diagnosed. A general component skipping malformed INPUT is ARC-F2D; a lookup table missing entries so a fallback value is silently used is COD-C3B; a scan tool losing coverage this way is SEC-G2B.
examples: Unregistered tool output formats silently skip instead of raising or logging
Generic host model resolution returns None instead of a diagnosable error when a host/role has no mapping
ARC-A4D.name: silent-failure-on-unrecognized-extension

lower_when.condition: The unregistered key can only come from first-party code paths enumerated in the same module (no user-, plugin- or file-supplied keys reach the lookup).

ARC-A5A.criteria: Qualifies when a constant or structure is duplicated because no CANONICAL OWNER exists — a proper fix establishes a single authoritative definition that other sites import or alias from (a structural ownership change). When the finding is simply that a constant is defined in more than one place and the copies should be unified (per-instance), that is QAL-D1B.
examples: SEV_ORDER and PANELS redefined locally in synthesize.py and html_report.py instead of owned by evidence.py and aliased
GROUP_RE/_OUTFILE_RE regex panel-alternation lists hand-duplicated instead of derived from PANELS
RATE_HINTS is defined identically or near-identically in three separate scripts instead of one shared source
ARC-A5A.name: non-canonical-constant-duplication

lower_when.condition: All copies are in the same module.

raise_when.condition: The copies already disagree on at least one value and both are read on a live code path (cite ARC-G1B alongside).

ARC-A5B.criteria: Qualifies when a data structure is maintained by hand although it is fully and mechanically derivable from another structure in the codebase, so the fix replaces it with a derivation (a function or comprehension). When the second structure is a duplicate but cannot be derived, that is ARC-A3B or ARC-A5A; when it is a separate registry that needs enforced parity, that is ARC-A4C.
examples: dispatch.py's AGENT_NAME dict was a byte-for-byte parallel derivation of ROLE_FILES; replaced with agent_name(role) function
ARC-A5B.name: redundant-derived-structure

lower_when.condition: The derived structure is built once next to its source in the same block and both are immutable.

ARC-B1A.criteria: Qualifies when third-party packages imported by shipped code are not declared in the project's dependency manifest, so a clean install fails or depends on whatever happens to be installed already. A manifest with no build-system declaration is ARC-B1D; first-party modules resolved through sys.path hacks are ARC-A2C; a declared but unpinned build dependency is SEC-E2A.
examples: pyyaml, jsonschema, and pytest are imported and used throughout the project but never declared as dependencies in pyproject.toml
ARC-B1A.name: missing-dependency-manifest-declarations

lower_when.condition: Every import of the undeclared package is wrapped in an ImportError fallback that disables a feature with a clear message.

ARC-B1C.criteria: Qualifies when URLs in the PROJECT / PACKAGING MANIFEST (pyproject [project.urls] Homepage/Repository/Issues, package metadata) are stale — they point to an org or location the project no longer uses, misstating the project's published identity. A stale URL in ordinary docs or code is QAL-C1A; the same identifier hardcoded across several modules so copies diverge is ARC-E1C.
examples: pyproject.toml Homepage/Repository/Issues URLs point to a GitHub org the repo itself no longer uses
ARC-B1C.name: stale-project-metadata-urls

lower_when.condition: The stale URL redirects automatically to the project's current location.

ARC-B1D.criteria: Qualifies when a packaging manifest declares project metadata but omits the build-system declaration (or its ecosystem equivalent) needed to install it, so the package looks installable but is not. Undeclared runtime dependencies are ARC-B1A; an install path that bypasses the package manager by design is ARC-B1F.
examples: pyproject.toml declares rich PyPI-style [project] metadata but has no [build-system] table, so the package is not actually pip-installable
ARC-B1D.name: incomplete-build-system-declaration

ARC-B1E.criteria: Qualifies when a lint or format configuration declares a rule or limit and, in the same configuration, disables the rule that enforces it, so the declared standard is not enforced. A prose document contradicting itself is QAL-C2B; inconsistent per-line suppression annotations are QAL-F3B.
examples: ruff line-length=100 is declared but the rule that enforces it (E501) is explicitly listed in the ignore set
ARC-B1E.name: self-contradictory-lint-configuration

lower_when.condition: A formatter configured in the same project enforces the declared limit, so the disabled lint rule is redundant.

ARC-B1F.criteria: Qualifies when the documented install mechanism bypasses the ecosystem's package manager (symlinks, manual copies into tool directories), so versions, uninstall and dependency resolution are unmanaged. A manifest that cannot actually be installed is ARC-B1D.
examples: README documents symlink-based installation into agent skill directories instead of a pip package install
ARC-B1F.name: nonstandard-install-mechanism-bypasses-package-manager

ARC-B3A.criteria: Qualifies when the same code runs on materially different paths or versions across environments the project treats as equivalent (CI matrix vs shipped image, test vs production image, with vs without an optional container), so what is tested is not what ships. Per-host configuration lacking parity is ARC-E3C; tests that run only in some environments are TST-F1B.
examples: ci.yml tests Python 3.11-3.13 but the Dockerfile base image only uses 3.12, so tested versions never match the deployed one
Inconsistent security posture between production and test Docker images
Optional Docker container creates divergent code-execution paths depending on whether it's present
Asymmetric dispatch architecture across agent platforms (kimi/claude/openrouter hosts) gives some hosts capabilities others lack
ARC-B3A.name: divergent-execution-path-across-environments

lower_when.condition: The divergence is a patch or minor-version difference inside a version range the project declares as supported and tests at both ends.

ARC-B3B.criteria: Qualifies when one container image bundles many unrelated toolchains or scanners, so every consumer inherits the full size, attack surface and rebuild blast radius of all of them. Excess runtime privilege granted to a container is SEC-C1A; a downstream image built FROM this one is ARC-B3C.
examples: panopticon-tools Dockerfile installs 8+ language toolchains plus 10+ security scanners into one image
ARC-B3B.name: monolithic-multi-toolchain-image

lower_when.condition: The image is a multi-stage build and consumers pull only a slim final stage scoped to their own toolchain.

ARC-B3C.criteria: Qualifies when one image or build artifact is built FROM another mutable in-repo artifact (a :latest tag of a sibling image), so a failure or change upstream silently breaks or alters the downstream build; a true build cycle is the extreme case. A cyclic MODULE import is ARC-A2A; a mutable third-party base reference is SEC-E2C.
examples: Dockerfile.fixtures builds FROM panopticon-tools:latest, so a failed tools build silently breaks fixture validation
ARC-B3C.name: circular-build-dependency

lower_when.condition: The downstream build pins the upstream image by digest or is built in the same workflow run as the upstream.

ARC-C1A.criteria: Qualifies when a CI gate decides pass/fail from raw, pre-model data (such as raw tool severity) instead of the project's own verdict or confirmation model, so the gate's result silently disagrees with what the project itself would report. A gate that never runs because a path filter skips it is ARC-C1B; analyzer confidence conflated with severity inside the model is COD-C1A.
examples: The 'ingest findings and gate on HIGH/CRITICAL' CI step calls ingest_tools.ingest_dir() and filters on raw tool severity directly, bypassing the project's own evidence/confirmation model entirely
ARC-C1A.name: ci-gate-bypasses-domain-verdict-model

lower_when.condition: The gating step is non-blocking (continue-on-error, an advisory job, or not a required check).

ARC-C1B.criteria: Qualifies when a workflow's trigger paths filter omits inputs the job actually consumes (files a Dockerfile COPYs, sources a generator reads), so changes to those inputs ship without the job running. A regeneration check that exists nowhere is ARC-C1F; a lint job whose file globs exclude in-scope code is ARC-C1D; a test-selection filter that silently drops tests is TST-F2A.
examples: docker-publish.yml's trigger paths: filter doesn't cover everything the Dockerfile COPYs into the published image, so some changes ship unbuilt
ARC-C1B.name: ci-trigger-path-filter-incomplete

lower_when.condition: A scheduled or release-time run executes the same job with no paths filter before anything is published.

ARC-C1C.criteria: Qualifies when an integration path has tests, but no CI workflow runs them against the real dependency (real tool binaries, real services), so the integration is never verified in the pipeline. When the tests themselves mock or omit the integration, that is TST-A3A; when tests skip themselves on environment gates, that is TST-F1B.
examples: Phase-1 tool-adapter integration tests never execute with real tooling in any CI workflow
ARC-C1C.name: untested-integration-path-in-ci

lower_when.condition: A scheduled or pre-release job outside the PR pipeline runs the integration tests against real tooling.

ARC-C1D.criteria: Qualifies when a CI lint or static-check job's file globs or excludes leave in-scope source (scripts, top-level ops code) unchecked, so violations there never fail CI. A trigger paths filter that skips the whole job is ARC-C1B; a test-selection filter that silently drops tests is TST-F2A.
examples: Top-level ops scripts that call the GitHub API are excluded from the CI lint job's file globs
ARC-C1D.name: ci-lint-gate-scope-gap

lower_when.condition: The excluded files are checked by a separate CI job or pre-commit hook enforced in CI.

raise_when.condition: The excluded files call remote write APIs or handle credentials, and the lint job runs security rules (e.g. a bandit or semgrep ruleset) that would otherwise check them.

ARC-C1E.criteria: Qualifies when a CI workflow omits the explicit least-privilege permissions block that its sibling workflows declare, so it runs with the platform's default token scope. A mutable action reference is SEC-E2B; excessive container privilege is SEC-C1A.
examples: ci.yml is the only in-scope workflow with no explicit least-privilege permissions: block, unlike codeql.yml/security.yml/docker-publish.yml
ARC-C1E.name: inconsistent-workflow-permissions-scoping

lower_when.condition: Settings-as-code or repository documentation in the reviewed tree shows the default GITHUB_TOKEN permission is read-only.

raise_when.condition: The workflow is triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run and checks out or executes code from the triggering fork PR.

ARC-C1F.criteria: Qualifies when a generated artifact (a JSON/Go/OpenAPI file derived from a generator source) is committed but no CI or build step regenerates it and fails on a diff, so a stale artifact ships silently. Does not qualify if a regeneration check exists but is skipped by a path filter — that is ARC-C1B.
examples: A committed generated artifact (engine_traits.json, servicelist.go, an OpenAPI spec) has no CI/build step that regenerates it and fails on a diff against its generator source, so a stale artifact ships silently
ARC-C1F.name: generated-artifact-drift-unverified-in-build

lower_when.condition: The shipped build regenerates the artifact from source, so the committed copy is used only for reading or review.

ARC-C2A.criteria: Qualifies when a pipeline step that fails silently falls back to an alternate path (a local rebuild, a cached artifact) with no failure signal, so an upstream breakage such as an incomplete publish is masked. A step whose failure is simply ignored is ARC-C2B; a scan tool that silently loses coverage is SEC-G2B; runtime error-swallowing in shipped code is OPS-E1A.
examples: security.yml silently falls back to a local docker build if pulling the pre-built panopticon-tools image fails, masking incomplete publishes
ARC-C2A.name: silent-fallback-masks-pipeline-failure

raise_when.condition: The fallback path builds or publishes a shipped artifact from inputs that differ from the primary path's.

ARC-C2B.criteria: Qualifies when a CI step is configured to ignore its own failure (continue-on-error, || true) with no compensating report, so a failed step is silently accepted. When the failure triggers a silent alternate path, that is ARC-C2A; a test runner exit code that conflates pass with no-op is TST-F2B.
examples: The merge job's build-provenance attestation step runs with continue-on-error: true, so a failed attestation is silently accepted
ARC-C2B.name: swallowed-ci-step-failure

raise_when.condition: The swallowed step is an integrity step (attestation, signing, vulnerability scan) whose failure lets an unverified artifact publish.

ARC-D1A.criteria: Qualifies when a producer transforms data on one path (scrubbing, normalizing, re-keying) and the recovery or read-back path does not apply the same transform, so recovered keys or records silently fail to match the originals. A one-off identifier normalization mismatch at a single lookup is COD-C2D; an identity that is unstable across runs is ARC-D1C.
examples: file_issues.py scrubs absolute paths when posting to GitHub, but the ledger-recovery fallback doesn't apply the same scrub, so recovered keys silently fail to match findings with absolute-path locations
ARC-D1A.name: lossy-round-trip-between-producer-and-recovery-path

lower_when.condition: A mismatch surfaces loudly (an error, or a duplicate-detection warning) instead of as a silent miss.

ARC-D1B.criteria: Qualifies when the schema and the documented contract are WHOLESALE out of sync — multiple fields or behaviors diverge across the two specs at once, so the contract as a whole is unreliable (a systemic doc-vs-schema divergence). A single field carrying a value outside its enum is COD-D1A; a single documented-required field missing from the schema's required list is COD-D1D.
examples: report-schema.json is materially out of sync with the documented report contract (INCONCLUSIVE status, coverage_certified, and other fields SKILL.md/panel-review.md/lens-sweep.md describe but the schema doesn't match)
ARC-D1B.name: report-contract-out-of-sync-with-schema

lower_when.condition: No producer or consumer validates against the schema at runtime or in CI.

ARC-D1C.criteria: Qualifies when an identity or fingerprint used to match the same finding or record across runs or systems is derived from unstable inputs (LLM free text, unordered data) or has an unspecified collision rule, so the same entity gets different ids. When the producer and recovery paths apply different transforms to a stable key, that is ARC-D1A; dedup on a too-coarse key that merges distinct entries is COD-E1A.
examples: Fingerprint-based queue ID format lacks a formal specification and has undocumented collision-suffix behavior
Compare-mode fingerprint hashes LLM-authored free text, which is not stable across runs of the same underlying finding
ARC-D1C.name: fingerprint-identity-instability

lower_when.condition: The id is used only for display or linking, never for matching, dedup or closure.

raise_when.condition: The id is the key for automatic issue closure or mark-as-resolved reconciliation, so an id change closes or resolves a still-present finding with no human review.

ARC-D1D.criteria: Qualifies when the SAME id or format is specified inconsistently across two or more specification artifacts (a schema pattern, a prompt template, a validator), and either none is authoritative or the declared authority has itself drifted from the others, so the contract has no single trustworthy format authority, regardless of whether any one instance is rejected. A live schema that actively rejects real output is COD-D1B; inert over-precision that rejects nothing is QAL-C2A; a dead, unimported stricter duplicate is QAL-E1B; a format specified only by an informal parser is ARC-A2B.
examples: Finding-ID regex diverges between agent prompt templates and the report schema
ARC-D1D.name: id-format-schema-mismatch

lower_when.condition: Only human-facing prose artifacts disagree; no prompt template, schema or validator that a producer or checker reads is among the disagreeing artifacts.

ARC-D1E.criteria: Qualifies when one runtime fact (coverage, counts, status) is computed independently from two or more sources with no reconciliation step, so the derivations can disagree and nothing notices. When two sources have ALREADY diverged, cite ARC-G1B; a hand-kept structure that could be derived from another is ARC-A5B; a mirror store contradicting its system of record is DAT-E1D.
examples: Fan-out coverage is derived from multiple independent sources that could disagree with no reconciliation step
ARC-D1E.name: redundant-independent-derivation-of-shared-fact

lower_when.condition: All derivations are reported side by side in the output, so a disagreement is visible to the reader.

ARC-D1F.criteria: Qualifies when phases or processes within one run exchange structured artifacts (JSON passed between pipeline stages) with no version field or compatibility check, so a producer change is silently misread by a mismatched consumer. When the artifact outlives the run (it is persisted and later resumed, replayed or compared by a different version), that is DAT-F2A.
examples: Pipeline phase coordination (scout -> dispatch -> synthesize) relies on JSON artifact contracts with no version field
ARC-D1F.name: unversioned-inter-phase-data-contract

lower_when.condition: Producer and consumer always run from the same checkout within one process invocation.

ARC-D2A.criteria: Qualifies when the CLI's declared interface contract as a whole has drifted from the implementation — the invocation syntax or the arguments manifest is structurally unreliable as a spec (systemic interface drift), not one stray line. A single documented flag that is entirely UNIMPLEMENTED is COD-D2B (a following user's run breaks); a specific stale or renamed flag description on an otherwise-implemented CLI is QAL-C2C (doc hygiene).
examples: Frontmatter arguments list covers only 4 of roughly 13 documented CLI flags
ARC-D2A.name: cli-interface-contract-drift

lower_when.condition: The drifted manifest or frontmatter is documentation only; no tool parses it to build or validate invocations.

ARC-D2B.criteria: Qualifies when inputs the contract treats as equivalent (missing vs present-but-empty, null vs absent) take different code paths with different outcomes, and the contract documents no rationale, so the contract is ambiguous at its edges. When one of the paths crashes, that is COD-B2A; a missing test for the boundary case is TST-A2D.
examples: enrich_citations derives citation_quality differently depending on whether a finding's citations field is missing versus present-but-empty, with no documented rationale for the distinction
ARC-D2B.name: inconsistent-handling-of-equivalent-edge-case-inputs

lower_when.condition: Both outcomes look the same to every downstream consumer (e.g. both render or serialize as empty).

ARC-D2C.criteria: Qualifies when two or more agents or processes write to shared state with no defined coordination contract (ownership, ordering, locking), so their writes can conflict or be misread. An unsynchronized shared structure inside one process is COD-F1C; concurrent file writes that lose updates are DAT-F1C; ambiguous spec text about which state applies is ARC-D2F.
examples: No defined coordination mechanism exists between lens_sweep and panel_review agents despite both writing to shared state
Panel-review lens-coverage fallback text conflates two opposite dispatch states, leaving readers unable to tell which one applies
ARC-D2C.name: missing-coordination-contract-between-agents

lower_when.condition: The agents run strictly one after another by construction (enforced ordering in the orchestrator), so writes cannot interleave.

ARC-D2D.criteria: Qualifies when a schema declares an optional field (or a family of fields) that no producer instruction or code ever populates, so the feature it was built to support is dead. A REQUIRED field never emitted is ARC-D2E; a configuration setting nothing reads is QAL-E1A.
examples: The scout prompt never populates several ScopeProfile fields, orphaning the facet feature the schema was built to support
ARC-D2D.name: orphaned-schema-field-never-populated

lower_when.condition: The schema documents the field as reserved for a future or optional producer.

ARC-D2E.criteria: Qualifies when a schema marks a field required but the producer's specification (prompt, template, code path) never instructs or emits it, so conforming output is impossible by construction. An observed output instance missing the field is COD-C3A; a documented-required field absent from the schema's required list (the inverse) is COD-D1D; an optional field never populated is ARC-D2D.
examples: report-schema.json requires findings[].confidence but neither lens-sweep.md nor panel-review.md ever instructs agents to write it
ARC-D2E.name: required-field-never-emitted-by-producer

lower_when.condition: Nothing in the pipeline validates output against this schema.

ARC-D2F.criteria: Qualifies when a spec or instruction uses a term, step or option it never defines, or describes one ambiguously enough that two readers (or agents) would act differently. One document stating both X and not-X is QAL-C2B; two documents contradicting each other is ARC-G1B; an omission from a reference inventory is ARC-G1C.
examples: Pipeline step 5 (plan dispatch) is ambiguous about single-group vs. multi-group invocation of dispatch.py
'repo-scope' is used but never defined in architecture panel scheduling docs
Scout's default-lens cheat sheet omits the redteam panel that the same document instructs it to schedule under security_mode=redteam
ARC-D2F.name: undefined-or-ambiguous-spec-terminology

lower_when.condition: The ambiguity is in human-facing prose only and no agent prompt or automated step reads the passage.

ARC-D3A.criteria: Qualifies when a file the CODE or BUILD references is absent, so something breaks (an import, include, or build step fails). Per the domain-routing principle this is the breaking case; a file mentioned only in DOCUMENTATION that is absent but breaks nothing is the inert ARC-D3B.
examples: skill/reference/codex-runner-instructions.md is referenced by scope assignment but does not exist in the repository
skill/reference/findings-envelope-schema.json is referenced but does not exist
ARC-D3A.name: missing-referenced-file

lower_when.condition: The missing file is referenced only by an optional, opt-in code path (a non-default flag or mode), so default runs never touch it.

ARC-D3B.criteria: Qualifies when documentation asserts a structural artifact or component the repository should contain — a directory, a process-backing file, an expected deliverable — that is absent, so the documentation and the repository's actual structure disagree (a doc-vs-repo disagreement → the architecture home per the routing principle), even though nothing breaks at build or runtime. A file referenced by CODE or BUILD whose absence breaks something is ARC-D3A; a specific file-PATH pointer that merely drifted out of date (a link or reference that no longer resolves) is the inert QAL-C1C.
examples: README's Repository layout table lists a docs/ directory that does not exist in this checkout
Documented security-disclosure process tells reporters to file a private advisory, but no SECURITY.md exists anywhere in the repo
ARC-D3B.name: documented-artifact-not-present-in-repo

lower_when.condition: The documentation marks the artifact as planned or optional.

ARC-E1A.criteria: Qualifies when shipped source hardcodes an absolute filesystem path tied to one machine or checkout (a user home directory, a mount point), so the code fails or misbehaves anywhere else. A relative but run- or date-specific artifact path is ARC-E1B; a machine-specific path in test fixture data is TST-E2C; a path resolved against the wrong base directory is COD-E2B.
examples: REPO_ROOT is a hardcoded absolute filesystem path baked into production code, breaking on any other machine or checkout location
ARC-E1A.name: hardcoded-absolute-path-in-source

lower_when.condition: The hardcoded path is only a default that an environment variable or CLI flag overrides.

ARC-E1B.criteria: Qualifies when code hardcodes the path or URL of one specific run's or date's artifact, so the tool cannot be reused for any other run without editing source. A machine-specific absolute path is ARC-E1A; the same identifier copied across several modules is ARC-E1C.
examples: DOC and DOC_URL hardcode a specific date-stamped artifact path (docs/superpowers/2026-08-04-run2-fixmes.md), preventing reuse for any other run
ARC-E1B.name: hardcoded-environment-specific-artifact-path

lower_when.condition: A CLI argument or config value overrides the hardcoded artifact path.

ARC-E1C.criteria: Qualifies when the same identifier (repo slug, org, resource path) is hardcoded INDEPENDENTLY in two or more modules with no single source of truth, so the copies can and do diverge — the scatter is the hazard, whether or not any copy is currently stale. A single out-of-date URL is staleness: QAL-C1A for doc/code references, ARC-B1C for packaging-manifest URLs.
examples: The GitHub repo slug is hardcoded independently in file_fixmes.py's DOC_URL and file_issues.py's REPORT_URL and has already diverged between them
